authorization: 2026-10-20 user (verbatim): 授权训练，删除那四个旧容器，用GPU 6,7,8,9. Authorizes the four arms x 1500000 steps of this configuration, removal of four never-started LM containers, and GPUs 6, 7, 8, 9 despite other projects' container reservations.
question: Under answer/EOS cross-entropy only, does an InfiLoop-style normalized carry with a relabeling-invariant score keep the ungated DiscoLoop's graph-B composition and round stability while removing the 1/r freezing of the additive carry, and does an identity-readable score instead reproduce the graph-specific timetable of the learned u gate?

input_origin.reuse: Exact existing 40000-example world and 43000-query panels used by every DiscoLoop/gate multi-hop arm

paired_recipe.note: Every arm's backbone at step 0 must equal the reused ungated DiscoLoop's step-0 model; handoff parameters are created without consuming the global RNG.

A0-discoloop-old-recipe.recipe: fixed R=4, final-round answer/EOS CE, constant LR after warmup, AdamW betas (0.9, 0.999), no EMA, CUDA graph

primary: At the 1500000-step endpoint with EMA weights: graph-B two/three/four-hop full-vocabulary answer accuracy at R8 from the R1-32 trace; also R4, R16, R32, graph-A held-out four-hop, all 11 panels, answer+EOS at R4/8/16/32, raw weights, and the full learning curves at R4/R8. No best checkpoint or horizon is selected.

comparisons.recipe: recipe-additive vs reused A0: InfiLoop-style training (random rounds, deep supervision, cosine LR, beta2 0.95, EMA) with the unchanged DiscoLoop handoff
comparisons.carry: ema vs recipe-additive: normalized convex carry with constant score versus additive carry, same recipe
comparisons.content_score: content vs ema: InfiLoop's identity-readable pseudo-query score
comparisons.invariance: invariant vs content: relabeling-invariant score versus identity-readable score

predictions.freezing: If additive accumulation freezes the carry, ema/content/invariant keep the answer-position relative change from decaying as 1/r beyond the trained rounds, and graph-B four-hop or graph-A held-out four-hop can rise with R; recipe-additive keeps the 1/r law. If all four stay flat with R, extra-round failure is not explained by the carry.
predictions.invariance: If identity-readable acceptance causes graph misalignment, content shows different gamma timetables for graph A and graph B at the same question type and round and lower graph-B composition than invariant; invariant shows matching timetables by construction when decode statistics match.
predictions.recipe_only: If recipe-additive already removes the +1-round transient and checkpoint drops while keeping graph-B composition, the architecture change is not needed for those properties; this is a valid outcome.

limits: One previously observed development world and one initialization; queries, rounds and checkpoints are not independent worlds.
Learned absolute positions cover only the trained length (sequence 6), so five-hop or longer questions are not tested in this batch; extra rounds on 1-4 hops are.
The training recipe changes as a package (random rounds, deep supervision, cosine LR, beta2, EMA); recipe-additive isolates the package, not each element.
Deep supervision sums the segment losses into one update per batch instead of InfiLoop's one update per segment, so update counts and exposures match A0.
The DiscoLoop decoded feedback is kept in every arm; it relies on next-token decodes being the intermediate entity in this template, which does not hold for natural-language questions.
Eager execution with random round counts is slower than A0's CUDA graph; wall time is not comparable.
Computation per update differs between arms and from A0; matrix FLOPs and executed rounds are logged for every update.
